rule: When the scalar multiplication reports a small-order public key, the endpoint MUST abandon the attempt, MUST NOT derive a session key, and MUST NOT create a mapping.
An endpoint MUST erase an ephemeral secret key, and every derived key, when the attempt or connection that owns it ends
Both endpoints MUST erase the shared secret as soon as the four keys are derived
MUST erase an ephemeral secret key when no handshake that needs it remains
the server MUST generate one for every mapping or take the current keypair of a bounded rotation window
A connection response that opens and whose padding is not all zero is `CONNECTION_RESPONSE_PADDING_NOT_ZERO`
A client that accepts a cookie MUST store its last 24 bytes and MUST send nothing in response.
A cookie accepted in sending connection request (2) MUST replace only the latest cookie
MUST ignore one whose echoed connection salt is not the attempt's salt
a denial in sending connection response (3) MUST open under the handshake server-to-client key the client already holds
The connection response is sealed and carries 24 zero bytes of padding.
A receiver MUST reject a packet type at or above the first reserved packet type as `RESERVED_TYPE`.
It MUST compare the computed value with the packet's filter value in constant time.
A sender and a receiver MUST each count, per connection and across all of that connection's keys, every sealed packet whose AEAD open fails.
On reaching the AEAD integrity limit below, the endpoint MUST end the connection
Refuse the packet without opening it when the sequence is at or below the high-water mark and its received bit is set.
The window depth is at least the `replay window depth minimum` and at most the `replay window depth maximum`
an implementation must not throttle application sends to preserve an assumed time span of history
Implementations must document their retained depth.
A receiver MUST bound this processing by its retained history, not by the number of sequence values asserted by the block.
Every lookup a server performs per packet or per connection must be constant time in the number of client slots.
The address and client-id lookups are hash tables, and the hash must be keyed with a secret generated at server start.
Each check MUST reject exactly the packets named for it
Pushing work down reduces the volume that reaches userspace rather than removing the check from it
A block that names a sequence always has a first range length of at least one
A sender MUST NOT name a sequence that it did not open.
A sender MUST construct ranges from the acknowledgement-eligible session-sequence state it maintains for the remote endpoint.
It is stated as a must because rules elsewhere depend on it
The sum of first range length and every gap and range length exceeds reconstructed largest received, so the lowest described sequence would be below sequence one.
The receiver MUST evaluate every remaining validity rule on that reconstructed value.
It MUST silently ignore sequences below its retained sent-history window.
When a block is malformed, a receiver MUST NOT apply its acknowledgements, examine the packet type data, refresh connection activity or add acknowledgement debt.
A sender MUST send a payload whose size is at most the payload capacity row of [t3 Constants and registries](#t3) as a type 5 packet
The schedule is driven by elapsed time, not by the number of application updates.
A sender MUST keep the send rate constant for the duration of one attempt.
An endpoint MUST expose the state of each connection and the reason a connection ended.
it MUST abandon the attempt for connect token expired (-7) once the token's lifetime, the difference between its expire timestamp and its create timestamp, has elapsed since the attempt began
The handshake and session sending sequences MUST start at one and MUST NOT be reset within the attempt.
A client that accepts a cookie MUST store its last 24 bytes
Ordinary traffic MUST NOT suppress this keep-alive.
A server MUST require a valid return cookie before any asymmetric work
The token identifier MUST be the BLAKE2b hash, of the `token identifier` size of [t3 Constants and registries](#t3) and with no key, of the signed connect data.
Comparisons must be constant time.
A mapping without a connected slot MUST be removed at its handshake deadline, which is fixed at creation and is never refreshed
An implementation must document the ratio it chose.
an implementation must document its capacity and eviction policy
A server MUST bind the token identifier to the source address at that point
A server MUST then refuse a token whose expire timestamp is not later than the server's current time
A server MUST take the claim at face value and MUST NOT wait for any other evidence before entering the regime of rule 2.
Entries expire with the tokens they name.
A server MUST send a keep-alive whenever the send rate interval has elapsed since it last sent that client a keep-alive, until a keep-alive it sent to that client has been acknowledged.
A sender MUST NOT name a sequence that it did not open.
The converse does not hold, and must not be assumed.
Any change to the ack block's encoding or validity rules, to the keep-alive's type data or size, or to the order in which the replay window is marked relative to those checks, must preserve it.
confirmation test must then be re-derived rather than assumed to still hold
It MUST zero all key material rather than merely mark the slot free.
a server config that names both families serves both, and a client on each family reaches connected
a server that names both families but serves only the first leaves the other family's client unconnected
